Events: all four propositions are one-step events and the transitions treat them as such; the u0 guards are mutually exclusive and exhaustive (each later guard negates all earlier events) and both states carry else self-loops, so no-event steps and any events occurring in u1 are covered by else. Coincident events resolve correctly under ordered matching: a step with top_breach together with side_breach (possible per the environment) fires (u0, top_breach) -> u1 with -100, i.e., the primary violation dominates and skipping the kill/side terms on that step cannot inflate reward. Reachability/compactness: u0 is initial and final, trivially reachable; u1 is reachable because top breaches do occur (idle episodes breach from step ~31); two states is minimal for FINAL_STATES-based acceptance of a 'never' task. Reward safety: the only positive term, +0.2 per zombie_killed, is aligned (a killed zombie can never breach), bounded (~18-37 entries per episode, at most a few points total), and cannot offset the -100; every other reward is a penalty on a genuine event, so there is no exploit path. Format: STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_HEADERS all present, FINAL_STATES nonempty with u0 declared and accepting; transitions use only the four predicate/event propositions with '&' and '!'; each reward line matches a declared transition with an identical guard; unlisted else rewards default to 0, and u1 awarding 0 afterwards is acceptable since acceptance is already decided there. Minor note (non-blocking): side_breach is penalized once per step even when two side zombies breach together, which is the correct per-proposition semantics.
